status: Execution sort-group planning admitted; repeated compatibility serialization removed; full acceptance remains open
implementation: Sort planning computes partition/order keys once per item and restricts candidate search to the matching partition key. Descending order-key length preserves stable longest-prefix group selection without the unreachable sort-expression replacement branch.

Scoped planning admits expression directories, ordered references, sorting scratch, candidate maps, group records and keys. Equal immutable key strings reuse retained backing; per-key formatting scratch releases immediately.
Execution backends keep planning metadata in temporary child scopes, separate from retained result rows. Planning keys release once groups are built.
Sort-group counting now uses the compatible-group count directly, removing a redundant serialization and Set pass.

cases: Stable longest-prefix grouping and partition separation without input reordering
Measured exact planning peak succeeds and one byte below rejects
Oversized serialized sort expressions reject while preserving a sibling reservation
validation.recordBoundaryUpdate: Existing exact record tests now measure the combined peak including transient planning directories; they still independently assert the retained result-record charge.
validation.build: pnpm exec tsc -b passed before runtime checks and benchmarks
validation.limitations: Coverage, external conformance and full packaging were not refreshed for this change.

worker.scope: Includes real Parquet window-key, frame, value and resume routes in local workerd R2

performance.method: Two warmups and three timed samples; legacy pairwise baseline versus cached and admitted implementations, with identical group membership/order asserted on every run.
performance.tradeoff: Admitted planning has material CPU overhead for already-compatible plans. Equal-key reuse reduced peak storage in the compatible 1024-window experiment from 542850 to 133788 bytes; it did not remove formatting/admission CPU cost.
performance.limitations: Local planning kernels; baseline does not account for memory. No cloud-latency, VM-heap or across-the-board speedup claim.

remainingAcceptance: Explain/read-column/task-topology planning metadata, timestamp-bound arithmetic and other execution metadata still require complete admission review.
Legacy spill-read pre-allocation admission, delegated task intermediates, transactional spill cleanup and other source/operator gaps remain open.
Full concurrent mixed-job/adaptive scheduling acceptance and production Cloudflare total-memory evidence remain open.
Reservation accounting does not establish total VM heap, external backing or RSS limits.
Low-headroom alternatives for cached planning remain part of adaptive acceptance; no fallback guarantee is established by this change.
